title: Just, Already & Yet
description: Give concise updates about recently completed travel actions.
objectives: Give concise updates about recently completed travel actions.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to give concise updates about recently completed travel actions. The central language is present perfect with just, already, and yet. It belongs to the practical context of travel & accommodation. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: present perfect with just, already, and yet

blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the just, already & yet exchange.
This just, already & yet model adds a different detail or response.

blocks.english: Could you help me with this problem?
blocks.explanation: Use this question or response to keep the just, already & yet exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I've just checked in.” and “Has the bus arrived yet?” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: present perfect with just, already, and yet.
